parts.working: B1 encrypted/locked to account or device. B1 copies cannot be read by others.

stem: A school has a 50-computer licence for a science simulation program. The head teacher asks the IT technician to install it on the home laptops of the 12 science teachers as well.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain what the technician should check before doing this.
parts.answer: Whether the licence terms allow home use / installation on staff devices, and whether the number of installations would exceed 50 (some licences count every installation).
parts.working: B1 licence terms on home/off-site use. B1 limit on number of installations.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Calculate the total number of installations if all school computers and all teachers' laptops have the program.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Discuss the risks to a company of using unlicensed software on its computers.
parts.answer: Legal: fines, legal action and having to pay for all licences; possible criminal charges for managers. Security: unlicensed copies may contain malware, risking data theft. Operational: no updates or security patches; no technical support; software may stop working when detected. Reputation: customers and partners lose trust if it becomes public. Also: some may argue it saves money in the short term, but costs of being caught are greater. Conclusion.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid point; max 5 without a conclusion; full marks need a range of risk types.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between a single-user licence and a multi-user licence.
parts.answer: A single-user licence allows the software to be installed/used by one user on one computer; a multi-user licence allows a set number of users or computers (e.g. in a network) to use it.
parts.working: B1 each.

stem: A start-up in Karachi plans to use open-source software for its office tasks instead of buying commercial software.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Evaluate this plan.
parts.answer: Benefits: usually no licence fee; source code available so it can be adapted; large user communities for help; no restriction on number of installations (depending on licence). Drawbacks: may have less official technical support; staff may need training if they are used to commercial programs; file compatibility with customers' software may be an issue; licence conditions still apply (e.g. changes may have to be shared if distributed); updates depend on the community. Conclusion.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid point; max 4 if one-sided; 6th mark for conclusion.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Some older programs would only run if the original disc was in the drive. Explain how this protected the software and give one drawback for the user.
parts.answer: The program checked for a special code/feature on the original disc that ordinary copying could not reproduce; a copied installation would not run without the original disc. Drawback: the user had to keep the disc with them and could not run the software if it was lost or scratched / the computer had no disc drive.
parts.working: B1 check for original disc. B1 copies lack the feature so will not run. B1 drawback.

stem: Three friends share one paid account for an online music-making program, each logging in from their own computer.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain whether this is acceptable, and describe how the software company might detect and prevent it.
parts.answer: It is usually not acceptable: the subscription licence is for one user, so sharing breaks the terms and the company loses income. Detection/prevention (any two/three): limiting the number of devices or simultaneous logins on one account; checking the location/IP address of logins; requiring two-factor authentication to a single phone; device registration.
parts.working: B1 breaks licence/one-user terms. B1 unfair/loss of income. Up to 2 for detection/prevention methods.

author: HomiLabs

stem: A student in Islamabad writes a mobile game and uploads it to an app store.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two ways the student could protect the game from being copied.
parts.answer: Any two: include a licence agreement users must accept; require users to log in / activate with an account; encrypt or obfuscate the code; include a copyright notice; use the app store's licence-checking system.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one benefit to the student of copyright law.
parts.answer: It gives the student the legal right to control and earn money from the game, and to take action against anyone who copies it.
parts.working: B1

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: A newsletter for a cricket club in Sialkot contains a photograph that is 15 cm wide and 10 cm high. It must be resized so that it is 6 cm wide and the aspect ratio is maintained. Calculate the new height of the photograph.
parts.answer: 4 cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the aspect ratio of the photograph should be maintained when it is resized.
parts.answer: So that the image is not distorted/stretched or squashed; the proportions of the people and objects stay correct so the image still looks realistic/professional.
parts.working: 1 mark: image not distorted (stretched/squashed). 1 mark: proportions (width to height) stay the same / people and objects keep their correct shape.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student is editing an image of a market stall for a school magazine. Describe the difference between cropping the image and resizing the image.
parts.answer: Cropping removes unwanted parts from the edges of the image, so some content is lost and the remaining part is unchanged in scale. Resizing changes the size/dimensions of the whole image but keeps all of its content.
parts.working: 1 mark: cropping cuts away/removes part of the image (from the edges). 1 mark: resizing makes the whole image bigger or smaller with all content kept.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one reason why the student might crop the image.
parts.answer: e.g. to remove an unwanted person/object at the edge; to focus attention on the main subject (the stall); to change its shape to fit a space.
parts.working: 1 mark for one valid reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A digital photograph of the Badshahi Mosque is 1600 pixels wide and 1200 pixels high. It is to be reduced to 480 pixels wide for a web page, keeping the aspect ratio. Calculate the new height in pixels.
parts.answer: 360 pixels

parts.label: b
parts.text: Each pixel is stored using 3 bytes and the image is not compressed. Calculate the file size, in bytes, of the original image and of the reduced image.
parts.answer: Original 5 760 000 bytes; reduced 518 400 bytes

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the reduced image is more suitable for the web page.
parts.answer: It has a much smaller file size so the page loads/downloads faster and uses less bandwidth.
parts.working: 1 mark: smaller file → faster loading.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A word-processed leaflet for a dental clinic in Peshawar contains a paragraph about opening hours. Describe the steps needed to place the image clinic.jpg so that it is aligned with the right margin and the text of the paragraph wraps around it.
parts.answer: Place the cursor in the paragraph and insert the image from file (Insert → Picture → clinic.jpg); select the image and set text wrapping to square (or tight); drag/position the image so its right edge is aligned with the right margin (or set horizontal alignment: right, relative to margin).
parts.working: 1 mark: insert the picture from the file. 1 mark: set text wrapping to square/tight. 1 mark: align/position image to the right margin.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An image of a horse facing right is placed in a document. Explain the difference between reflecting the image horizontally and rotating it through 180°.
parts.answer: Reflecting (flipping) horizontally makes a mirror image so the horse faces left but stays the right way up. Rotating through 180° turns the image so the horse faces left and is also upside down.
parts.working: 1 mark: reflect = mirror image, horse now faces left, still upright. 1 mark: rotate 180° = horse upside down (and facing left).

parts.label: b
parts.text: The horse must face towards the text on the left of the page. State which of the two edits should be used.
parts.answer: Reflect (flip) horizontally.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An uncompressed image is 800 pixels wide and 600 pixels high. Its colour depth is 24 bits per pixel. Calculate its file size in bytes.
parts.answer: 1 440 000 bytes

parts.label: b
parts.text: The colour depth is reduced to 8 bits per pixel. Calculate the new file size in bytes and the number of different colours that can now be shown.
parts.answer: 480 000 bytes; 256 colours

parts.label: c
parts.text: Describe one effect on the appearance of the image of reducing the colour depth.
parts.answer: Fewer colours are available so smooth changes of colour (e.g. a sky) appear as bands/blocks of colour and some detail/realism is lost.
parts.working: 1 mark: fewer colours → banding / less realistic / loss of quality.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A travel agent in Lahore wants to reduce the file size of the photographs on her website. State three ways the file size of an image can be reduced.
parts.answer: Any three: reduce the resolution/number of pixels (resize it smaller); crop unwanted areas; reduce the colour depth; compress the image (e.g. save as a compressed .jpg at a lower quality).
parts.working: 1 mark each for any three distinct methods.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An image in a report is 9.3 cm wide and 12.4 cm high. It must be resized to exactly 8 cm high with the aspect ratio maintained. Calculate the new width, in centimetres.
parts.answer: 6 cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe how the student can make sure the aspect ratio is maintained when entering the new height in the software.
parts.answer: Tick/select the 'lock aspect ratio' (keep proportions) option before typing the new height, so the width changes automatically.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An image of the Karakoram mountains is 2000 pixels wide and 1500 pixels high. It is cropped by removing 250 pixels from the left and 250 pixels from the right, and 150 pixels from the top and 150 pixels from the bottom. Calculate the dimensions of the cropped image.
parts.answer: 1500 pixels wide × 1200 pixels high

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give the aspect ratio of the cropped image in its simplest form, width : height.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A photograph taken inside a dimly lit museum looks dark and dull: the dark areas and light areas look very similar. Explain the difference between adjusting the brightness and adjusting the contrast of an image.
parts.answer: Brightness makes every pixel in the whole image lighter (or darker) by the same amount. Contrast changes the difference between the light and dark areas: increasing it makes light areas lighter and dark areas darker.
parts.working: 1 mark: brightness = whole image lighter/darker. 1 mark: contrast = difference between light and dark parts.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State which adjustments should be made to improve this photograph, giving a reason for each.
parts.answer: Increase the brightness so that the details in the dark image can be seen; increase the contrast so that the light and dark areas are more clearly different/the image looks less dull.
parts.working: 1 mark: increase brightness + reason. 1 mark: increase contrast + reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An image is 1080 pixels wide and 720 pixels high. It is rotated 90° clockwise. State the width and height of the rotated image.
parts.answer: 720 pixels wide and 1080 pixels high
parts.working: B1: width and height swap.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one reason why an image taken with a phone might need to be rotated before it is used.
parts.answer: e.g. the phone was held sideways so the image appears on its side; to change it from landscape to portrait to fit a space.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A document for a book club contains three images. For each image, name the most suitable text wrapping setting.
(i) A logo that must sit on its own line above the title, with no text on either side.
(ii) A photograph in the middle of a paragraph, with the text running down both sides close to the outline of an irregular-shaped object.
(iii) A small icon that must move with the words in a line of text as if it were a character.
parts.answer: (i) Top and bottom; (ii) Tight (or through); (iii) In line with text.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A school in Multan is putting hundreds of photographs of school events on its website. The web designer plans to reduce the resolution of every photograph before uploading it. Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of reducing the resolution of the photographs.
parts.answer: Benefits: smaller file sizes so pages load faster, especially on mobile data; uses less storage space on the web server; uses less bandwidth so hosting may cost less; quicker to upload; less data used by visitors. Drawbacks: image quality/detail is lost; images may look pixelated if enlarged or viewed on large high-resolution screens; visitors cannot download good-quality versions to print; the reduction cannot be undone unless the originals are kept; it takes time to edit hundreds of photographs. Conclusion e.g. benefits outweigh drawbacks for a web page if originals are kept.
parts.working: Max 4 marks for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point from: faster loading; less server storage; less bandwidth/cost; faster upload; loss of detail; pixelation when enlarged; poor for printing; cannot undo/originals must be kept; time taken. 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion. Answers in prose comparing both sides needed for full marks.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The image fort.jpg is 900 pixels wide and 600 pixels high. On a web page it must be displayed 300 pixels wide with its aspect ratio kept. Calculate the height at which it must be displayed.
parts.answer: 200 pixels

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the HTML to display the image at this size, with the alternative text 'Lahore Fort'.
parts.working: 1 mark: img element with src="fort.jpg". 1 mark: width="300" and height="200" and alt="Lahore Fort". Accept the size given with a style attribute.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A graphic designer is preparing images for a charity website. State the most suitable generic file format for each image and give a reason.
(i) A colour photograph of a flood relief camp.
(ii) A logo that must have a transparent background so the page colour shows through.
(iii) A small, simple animated 'Donate' banner.
parts.answer: (i) .jpg — compressed format suited to photographs with many colours (small file). (ii) .png — supports transparency (and lossless compression keeps sharp edges). (iii) .gif — supports simple animation (limited colours suit a simple banner).
parts.working: 1 mark each: correct format with reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text: In a poster for a science fair, a photograph of a student has been made wider without changing its height. The student's face now looks stretched. Explain why this has happened and describe how to correct it.
parts.answer: The aspect ratio was not maintained, so the width was increased by a different factor from the height. To correct it: reset the image size (or undo), lock the aspect ratio, then resize by dragging a corner handle (or changing one dimension) so both dimensions change in proportion.
parts.working: 1 mark: aspect ratio not maintained / width changed but not height. 1 mark: reset or undo the distortion. 1 mark: lock aspect ratio / use corner handle so width and height change proportionally.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An image 2400 pixels wide and 1800 pixels high is scaled to 35% of its width and 35% of its height. Calculate the new dimensions.
parts.answer: 840 pixels × 630 pixels

parts.label: b
parts.text: The image is uncompressed. Calculate the new file size as a percentage of the original file size.

parts.label: c
parts.text: A student says 'scaling to 35% makes the file 35% of its original size'. Explain why the student is wrong.
parts.answer: Both the width and the height are reduced, so the number of pixels is multiplied by 0.35 twice (0.35 × 0.35), not once.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the steps needed to insert the image bus.png into a document so that it is exactly 5 cm wide, with its height in proportion, and placed at the top left of the first page below the header.
parts.answer: Position the cursor at the start of the document (top left, below the header) and insert the picture from the file bus.png; with aspect ratio locked, set the width to 5 cm (the height changes automatically); check the image is aligned with the left margin/top of the text area.
parts.working: 1 mark: insert picture from file at start of document. 1 mark: lock aspect ratio and set width to 5 cm. 1 mark: align to left margin at top of page.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A photograph is to be printed 6 inches wide and 4 inches high at 300 dots (pixels) per inch. Calculate the number of pixels needed across and down the image.
parts.answer: 1800 pixels across and 1200 pixels down

parts.label: b
parts.text: The photographer only has a version 900 pixels wide. Calculate the number of pixels per inch it would give if printed 6 inches wide, and explain the effect on the printed photograph.
parts.answer: 150 pixels per inch; the photograph would look less sharp/blurred or pixelated because each pixel is printed larger.
parts.working: B1: 900 ÷ 6 = 150. B1: less sharp / pixelated with reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A profile photograph is 1200 pixels wide and 900 pixels high. It must become a square image 250 pixels wide for a membership card, showing the person's face in the centre. Describe, with dimensions, the two edits needed and the order in which they should be done.
parts.answer: First crop the image to a square 900 × 900 pixels by removing 150 pixels from each side (left and right), keeping the face central. Then resize the square image, with aspect ratio locked, to 250 × 250 pixels.
parts.working: 1 mark: crop to 900 × 900 (remove 300 pixels of width). 1 mark: 150 pixels from each side to keep face centred. 1 mark: then resize to 250 × 250 with aspect ratio kept.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why resizing the original image straight to 250 × 250 pixels would not be suitable.
parts.answer: The original is 4 : 3, not square, so forcing it to 250 × 250 would distort/squash the face.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by the aspect ratio of an image.
parts.answer: The ratio of the width of the image to its height.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: An image is 640 pixels wide and 480 pixels high. Give its aspect ratio in its simplest form.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A table in a recipe booklet has a column that is 4.5 cm wide. A picture of a mango, 7.5 cm wide and 5 cm high, must fit exactly across the width of one cell with its aspect ratio maintained. Calculate the height of the resized picture.
parts.answer: 3 cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one reason why the picture should be resized in the document rather than stretched by dragging a side handle.
parts.answer: Dragging a side handle changes only one dimension so the picture is distorted; entering the size with the ratio locked keeps proportions and gives an exact width.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Complete the statements: the maximum number of different colours that can be represented with a colour depth of
(i) 1 bit
(ii) 4 bits
(iii) 8 bits
(iv) 16 bits.
parts.working: 2 marks for all four correct; 1 mark for two or three correct (2ⁿ).

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a photograph stored with a colour depth of 24 bits has a larger file size than the same photograph stored with 8 bits.
parts.answer: Each pixel needs 24 bits instead of 8, so three times as much data is stored for the same number of pixels.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An uncompressed image uses 3 bytes per pixel and has an aspect ratio of 4 : 3. Its file size must be no more than 600 KB, where 1 KB = 1024 bytes. Its width must be a multiple of 4 pixels. Calculate the largest possible width and height, and the file size in bytes at that size.
parts.answer: Width 520 pixels, height 390 pixels, file size 608 400 bytes

parts.label: a
parts.text: A scanned map has been inserted into a sports day flyer upside down: the north arrow and the labels point towards the bottom of the page. Name the image edit, including the angle, that will correct it.
parts.answer: Rotate the image through 180°.
parts.working: 1 mark: rotate 180°. Do not accept flip/reflect vertically (this would leave the labels as a mirror image).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one other edit, apart from resizing and cropping, that can be applied to an image in a document.
parts.answer: e.g. rotate; change brightness; change contrast; change colour depth/recolour; apply text wrapping.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain why images placed on web pages are usually compressed.
parts.answer: Compression reduces the file size so the image downloads faster and the web page loads more quickly; it also uses less bandwidth/storage on the server.
parts.working: 1 mark: smaller file size. 1 mark: faster loading / less bandwidth or storage.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Describe the difference between lossy and lossless compression of an image.
parts.answer: Lossy compression permanently removes some image data (detail the eye may not notice), so the original cannot be fully restored but the file is much smaller. Lossless compression reduces the file size without losing any data, so the original image can be restored exactly.
parts.working: 1 mark: lossy removes data permanently. 1 mark: lossless — no data lost / original restored exactly.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A newsletter is set on A4 portrait paper (21 cm wide). The left and right margins are each 2 cm. The page has two columns of equal width with 1 cm spacing between them. Calculate the width of each column.
parts.answer: 8 cm

parts.label: b
parts.text: An image 12 cm wide and 9 cm high must fill the full width of one column with its aspect ratio maintained. Calculate the new height.
parts.answer: 6 cm

parts.label: a
parts.text: A photograph of a wedding was taken outdoors in strong sunlight and looks too light, with faded colours. State which adjustment should be made.
parts.answer: Decrease the brightness (accept: also increase the contrast).
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one reason why the original photograph should be kept before editing.
parts.answer: So the edits can be undone / the original can be used again if the edit is not suitable, because some edits cannot be reversed once saved.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A page from an old school register has been scanned. The scanned image is tilted about 3° anticlockwise and has white triangles at its corners after it is straightened. Describe the two edits needed to produce a neat, straight rectangular image.
parts.answer: Rotate the image about 3° clockwise so the text lines are horizontal; then crop the image to remove the empty/white triangles at the corners.
parts.working: 1 mark: rotate 3° clockwise. 1 mark: crop to remove the corners/edges.

parts.label: a
parts.answer: Squashed: reset the size and resize with the aspect ratio locked (drag a corner handle). Overlaps margin: reduce the width (in proportion) or move it so it fits within the column/margins. Empty spaces: change text wrapping from top and bottom to square/tight. Covers header: move the image down into the body of the page (below the header) / anchor it in the text.
parts.working: 1 mark per correct fix for each problem (4).

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between a formula and a function in a spreadsheet.
parts.answer: A formula is a calculation entered by the user, using cell references, values and operators, e.g. =B2*C2. A function is a predefined/built-in named operation in the software that carries out a calculation on given arguments/a range, e.g. =SUM(B2:B10).
parts.working: 1 mark: formula = user-written calculation with operators/cell references. 1 mark: function = built-in/predefined named routine. Examples alone not enough.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one example of each, using cell references.
parts.answer: Formula e.g. =D4-E4 or =B3*1.17; function e.g. =AVERAGE(C2:C20) or =MAX(B2:B9).
parts.working: 1 mark for a valid formula; 1 mark for a valid function.

stem:

stem: An electronics shop stores the sales tax rate, 17%, in cell F1. Prices of items (Rs) are in B2 to B20.

parts.label: a

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why an absolute reference is needed in this formula.
parts.answer: When the formula is replicated, relative references change (B2 becomes B3, B4…) but the tax rate is always in F1, so the reference to F1 must not change; otherwise the formula would point to F2, F3… which are empty.

parts.text: State the grades shown for the percentages 80, 79, 65, 50 and 49.5.

stem:
A courier company stores a lookup table in H2:J6.
Column H code | Column I city | Column J charge (Rs)
KHI | Karachi | 250
LHE | Lahore | 300
ISB | Islamabad | 350
PEW | Peshawar | 400
QTA | Quetta | 450
Orders are in rows 2 to 50; column B holds each order's city code.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to look up the delivery charge for the city code in B2. It must work when replicated down column C.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(B2,$H$2:$J$6,3,FALSE)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP with B2 as lookup value. 1 mark: absolute range $H$2:$J$6. 1 mark: column 3 and FALSE (exact match). Accept 0 for FALSE; accept a named range.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B2 contains ISB. State the value displayed in C2.

parts.label: c
parts.text: B5 contains MUX. State what is displayed in C5 and explain why.
parts.answer: #N/A (an error); MUX is not in the first column of the lookup table and an exact match was requested.
parts.working: 1 mark: #N/A / error. 1 mark: reason.

author: HomiLabs

stem:
A wholesaler gives a discount based on the order value. The table in F2:G5 is:
F (order value from, Rs) | G (discount)
0 | 0%
5000 | 5%
10000 | 8%
20000 | 12%

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to find the discount rate for the order value in B2, using the table, so that it works when replicated.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(B2,$F$2:$G$5,2,TRUE)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP with B2 and absolute $F$2:$G$5. 1 mark: column 2 with TRUE (approximate match); accept TRUE omitted.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the discount rate given for order values of Rs 4999, Rs 10 000, Rs 17 500 and Rs 25 000.
parts.working: 2 marks all four; 1 mark for two or three.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Calculate the discount, in rupees, on an order of Rs 17 500.

parts.label: d
parts.text: Explain why the values in column F must be in ascending order.
parts.answer: An approximate-match lookup searches for the largest value that is less than or equal to the lookup value, which only works correctly if the first column is sorted in ascending order.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

stem:
A weather station's spreadsheet holds months in row 1 and rainfall (mm) in row 2.
B1:G1: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, May, Jun

parts.label: a

parts.working: 1 mark: HLOOKUP with "Mar" (or a cell containing Mar). 1 mark: range B1:G2. 1 mark: row 2 and FALSE.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write a function to find the total rainfall for the six months and state its value.

author: HomiLabs

stem: A pharmacy stock sheet has product codes in A2:A9, product names in B2:B9, prices in C2:C9 and stock levels in D2:D9.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a formula in H3 using XLOOKUP that displays the stock level for the product code typed in H2. If the code is not found, the cell must display Not found.
parts.answer: =XLOOKUP(H2,A2:A9,D2:D9,"Not found")
parts.working: 1 mark: XLOOKUP with H2 as lookup value. 1 mark: lookup array A2:A9 and return array D2:D9. 1 mark: "Not found" as the if-not-found argument.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State one advantage of XLOOKUP compared with VLOOKUP.
parts.answer: e.g. the return column can be to the left of the lookup column; it does not break if columns are inserted (no column number); exact match is the default; it has a built-in 'not found' value.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

(iii) =ROUNDDOWN(A1,2)

parts.text: A school in Faisalabad is taking 263 students on a trip. Each bus holds 45 students. The number of students is in B1 and the bus capacity in B2. Write a formula to calculate the number of buses needed, and state its value.

parts.text: An egg farm collects 1000 eggs (in C1). A tray holds 30 eggs (in C2). Write a formula to calculate the number of full trays and state its value.

stem: A club records the number of runs scored by a batter in B2 to B9. The cells contain: 12, absent, 15, (empty), 0, 18, absent, 9.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the value displayed by
(i) =COUNT(B2:B9)
(ii) =COUNTA(B2:B9)
parts.working: B1 each. COUNT counts the five numbers (12, 15, 0, 18, 9); COUNTA counts all seven non-empty cells.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the two values are different.
parts.answer: COUNT only counts cells containing numbers; COUNTA counts every cell that is not empty, including text such as 'absent'.
parts.working: 1 mark.

check: len([x for x in [12,'absent',15,'',0,18,'absent',9] if x != '' and x != 'absent']) == 5 and len([x for x in [12,'absent',15,'',0,18,'absent',9] if x != '']) == 7
author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: Cell B1 contains the exchange rate 278.50 (rupees per US dollar). The cell is given the name Rate. Write the formula in C5 to convert the dollar amount in B5 to rupees using the named cell.
parts.answer: =B5*Rate
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: B5 contains 40. State the value displayed in C5.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Give two advantages of using a named range rather than the cell reference $B$1.
parts.answer: Any two: formulas are easier to read/understand; easier to enter without errors; the name acts as an absolute reference so it does not change when the formula is replicated; the range can be found/edited easily.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Cell D2 contains the formula =B2*C2. It is replicated down to D5. Write the formula that will be in D5.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Cell E2 contains =D2*$G$1. It is replicated down to E5. Write the formula that will be in E5.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain the difference between relative and absolute cell referencing.
parts.answer: A relative reference changes to match its new position when the formula is copied/replicated. An absolute reference (with $ signs) always refers to the same cell however it is copied.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

stem: A mixed-reference times table: B1:D1 contain 5, 6, 7 and A2:A4 contain 2, 3, 4. B2 contains =$A2*B$1 and is replicated to fill B2:D4.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in D4 after replication.

stem: A family in Rawalpindi records monthly electricity bills (Rs) in B2:B13 for January to December. The bills for November and December have not arrived, so B12 and B13 are empty. B2:B11 contain 8450, 7920, 9310, 11240, 13680, 15020, 14760, 12890, 10330, 9050.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State the value displayed by =AVERAGE(B2:B13).
parts.working: B1: 112 650 ÷ 10 = 11 265 (blank cells ignored).

parts.label: b
parts.text: State the value displayed by =SUM(B2:B13)/12.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Explain why the two results are different and state which one gives the correct mean bill so far.
parts.answer: AVERAGE ignores the two empty cells and divides by 10 (the number of bills); SUM/12 divides by 12 including the months with no bill. AVERAGE gives the correct mean of the bills received.
