author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text: A sheet calculates the cost per student of a club using =B2/C2, where B2 holds the total cost and C2 the number of students. When C2 is 0 the cell shows #DIV/0!. Explain why.
parts.answer: The formula is trying to divide by zero, which cannot be calculated.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula that displays No students when C2 is 0 and otherwise shows the cost per student.
parts.answer: =IF(C2=0,"No students",B2/C2)
parts.working: 1 mark: IF testing C2=0 with "No students". 1 mark: B2/C2 as false value.

stem: A student records the daily rainfall (mm) in Murree for 10 days in B2:B11: 0, 4.5, 0, 12, 0, 0, 7.2, 1.1, 0, 3.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a function to count the number of days on which some rain fell, and state its value.
parts.working: 1 mark function; B1: 5.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula to calculate the proportion of days with rain, using COUNTIF and COUNT, and state the result as a percentage.
parts.answer: =COUNTIF(B2:B11,">0")/COUNT(B2:B11); 50%
parts.working: 1 mark formula; B1: 5 ÷ 10 = 50%.

author: HomiLabs

stem: A student's bank transactions (Rs) are in B2:B9. Deposits are positive and withdrawals negative: 5000, −1200, −350, 2500, −800, 1500, −2000, 700.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write a function to calculate the total of all the withdrawals (negative values) and state its value.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write a formula using SUMIF and COUNTIF to calculate the mean deposit (positive values) and state its value.
parts.working: 1 mark formula; B1: 9700 ÷ 4 = 2425.

parts.label: c
parts.text: Write a single function that gives the same result as the formula in (b).
parts.answer: =AVERAGEIF(B2:B9,">0")
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
A sports coach keeps players' sprint times in a spreadsheet. Name the most suitable function for each task.
(i) Find the fastest (lowest) time.
(ii) Find how many times have been entered.
(iii) Find how many players are in the 'Under 16' group.
(iv) Show 'Selected' if a time is below 12 seconds, otherwise 'Not selected'.
parts.answer: (i) MIN (ii) COUNT (iii) COUNTIF (iv) IF
parts.working: 1 mark each.

stem: A garden centre's sheet has a named range Prices covering a table: column 1 product code, column 2 product name, column 3 unit price (Rs). The discount rate for loyal customers is in cell H1.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Write the formula in C2 to calculate the cost of the order: look up the unit price of the product code in A2 from the Prices range, multiply by the quantity in B2 and apply the discount in H1. It must work when replicated.
parts.answer: =VLOOKUP(A2,Prices,3,FALSE)*B2*(1-$H$1)
parts.working: 1 mark: VLOOKUP(A2,Prices,…). 1 mark: column 3, FALSE. 1 mark: ×B2. 1 mark: ×(1−$H$1) with absolute reference. Accept equivalent e.g. −…*$H$1.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A2 contains F07, whose unit price is Rs 1240. B2 contains 3 and H1 contains 10%. State the value displayed in C2.

author: HomiLabs

parts.label: a
parts.text:
B2 contains the population 1284567 and B3 contains 739421. State the value displayed by
(i) =ROUND(B2,-3)
(ii) =ROUND(B3,-3)
(iii) =ROUND(B2,-5)
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain what the negative number in =ROUND(B2,-3) does.
parts.answer: It rounds to the left of the decimal point, here to the nearest thousand.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A teacher wants C2 to show Pass when the mark in B2 is 50 or more. She has entered =IF(B2>50,"Pass","Fail"). Give a test value for B2 that would show the formula is wrong, and state the output it gives and the output expected.
parts.answer: 50; it displays Fail but Pass is expected.
parts.working: 1 mark: 50 (the boundary). 1 mark: Fail given, Pass expected.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Write the corrected formula.
parts.answer: =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail")
parts.working: 1 mark. Accept =IF(B2<50,"Fail","Pass").

parts.label: c
parts.text: Marks are whole numbers from 0 to 100. Give two further test values, other than your answer to (a), that test the corrected formula on each side of the boundary, with the expected output for each.
parts.answer: 49 → Fail; 51 → Pass (accept e.g. 0 → Fail, 100 → Pass with explanation as extreme data).
parts.working: 1 mark each: value with correct expected output.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A weather station in Gilgit records the air temperature and rainfall every 10 minutes. A greenhouse near Quetta keeps its temperature between 22 °C and 26 °C. Explain why the weather station is an example of a monitoring system and the greenhouse is an example of a control system.
parts.answer: The weather station only takes/records/displays readings from sensors and does not change anything. The greenhouse system uses the readings to switch devices (heater, fan, window motor) on or off through actuators to change the conditions.
parts.working: 1 mark: monitoring = readings recorded/displayed, no action taken. 1 mark: control = computer uses readings to operate actuators/devices to change conditions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Name two sensors, other than temperature sensors, that could be used in the greenhouse.
parts.answer: Any two: humidity/moisture sensor; light sensor; soil moisture sensor; pH sensor; CO₂/gas sensor.
parts.working: 1 mark each. Do not accept brand names or 'heat sensor'.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A hatchery in Punjab uses a microprocessor-controlled incubator to keep eggs at 37.5 °C. Describe how the microprocessor controls the temperature.
parts.answer: A temperature sensor constantly measures the temperature; the analogue reading is converted to digital by an ADC; the microprocessor compares the reading with the preset value (37.5 °C) stored in memory; if it is lower, a signal is sent (through a DAC/actuator) to switch the heater on (and fan off); if it is higher, the heater is switched off/the fan is switched on; this process repeats continuously.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any five: sensor measures temperature; ADC converts analogue to digital; compares with preset value; below → heater on; above → heater off/fan on; actuator/DAC used to operate device; process continuous loop.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An environmental agency wants to monitor the pollution level in the River Ravi at 20 points along its length. It is choosing between using computers with sensors and sending staff to take readings by hand. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of using computers with sensors.
parts.answer: Advantages: readings can be taken 24 hours a day and at regular, precise intervals; readings are more accurate/no human error; staff do not need to visit dangerous or polluted places; results can be sent automatically and analysed/graphed immediately; sudden pollution events are noticed quickly and alarms can be raised; cheaper in staff costs in the long term. Disadvantages: high initial cost of sensors, computers and communication links; sensors can be damaged, stolen or fouled and need maintenance/calibration; power failure or a fault may lose data; staff may lose jobs or need retraining. Conclusion weighing both sides.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded valid point; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion. Answers must refer to the river scenario for full marks.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
For each application, name the most suitable sensor.
(i) Detecting a person walking past a shop's automatic door.
(ii) Switching on street lights when it gets dark.
(iii) Detecting when a car is waiting at a traffic light.
(iv) Measuring the acidity of water in a fish farm.
parts.answer: (i) infrared/motion sensor (ii) light sensor (iii) pressure sensor (or magnetic field/induction loop sensor) (iv) pH sensor
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A family in Karachi books cinema tickets online. Give three advantages to the family of booking online rather than at the cinema box office.
parts.answer: Any three: can book at any time of day; no need to travel to the cinema to book/no queuing; can see the seat plan and choose the seats they want; can compare times/prices easily; e-ticket sent to phone so no paper ticket to lose; may get special online offers.
parts.working: 1 mark each for three distinct advantages. Do not accept 'quicker' or 'easier' without a reason.

parts.label: a
parts.text: An airline's online booking system must make sure the same seat is never sold to two customers. Describe how the system does this.
parts.answer: When a customer selects a seat, the system checks the central database that it is available; the seat is temporarily held/locked for that customer while they complete payment so no one else can select it; when payment is completed the database is updated immediately (real-time processing) so the seat shows as booked; if payment is not completed within a time limit, the seat is released.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four: checks availability in database; seat locked/held during transaction; database updated immediately/real-time; other users see seat as unavailable; seat released after timeout.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A concert organiser in Lahore is closing its box office and will sell all tickets through an online booking system. Discuss the benefits and drawbacks to the organiser.
parts.answer: Benefits: fewer box-office staff so lower wage costs; tickets sold 24/7 to customers worldwide; real-time seat availability prevents double booking; payments received immediately/electronically; customer data collected for marketing; e-tickets reduce printing costs; sales reports instantly available. Drawbacks: cost of setting up/maintaining the website and booking software; customers without internet access/cards may not buy tickets, losing sales; risk of hacking/data breach and fake websites; system crash on busy release days loses sales/reputation; staff made redundant; fees charged by payment providers. Conclusion.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car factory near Karachi uses robots to weld and spray-paint car bodies. Give three advantages to the factory of using robots for these tasks.
parts.answer: Any three: robots can work 24 hours a day without breaks; every weld/coat of paint is the same/consistent quality; more accurate than humans; no wages to pay/lower running costs; can work in dangerous environments (fumes, sparks) so workers are safer; higher productivity.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one disadvantage to the factory of using robots.
parts.answer: e.g. very expensive to buy and install; need regular maintenance/specialist technicians; cannot adapt to unexpected situations; a breakdown can stop the production line.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A large online shop uses robots in its warehouse to fetch shelves of goods and bring them to human packers. Describe how the robots can move around the warehouse safely and find the correct shelves.
parts.answer: Robots are controlled by a central computer that sends them the location of the required shelf; they navigate using sensors such as cameras/barcodes or markers on the floor (or GPS-like indoor positioning); proximity/infrared/ultrasonic sensors detect obstacles or people so the robot slows or stops; the robot reads the shelf's barcode/RFID tag to confirm it is the correct shelf before lifting it.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four valid points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A textile factory in Faisalabad plans to replace many of its machine operators with robots. Discuss the effects of this decision on the factory's workers.
parts.answer: Negative: many operators may lose their jobs (unemployment); remaining workers may have to retrain; work may become deskilled/repetitive supervision; fear and lower morale. Positive: new jobs for robot programmers, technicians and maintenance staff; workers removed from noisy, dusty or dangerous tasks so fewer injuries; retrained workers may earn higher wages; more interesting supervisory work; shorter hours possible. Conclusion.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion. Answers must be about workers, not the factory's profits.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name four components of an expert system.
parts.answer: Any four: knowledge base; rules base; inference engine; user interface; explanation system.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A farmer uses an expert system to identify a disease affecting her wheat crop. Describe how the expert system produces a diagnosis.
parts.answer: The user interface asks the farmer questions about the symptoms (e.g. colour of leaves, spots); the farmer answers, often by choosing yes/no or from options; the inference engine uses the rules base to compare the answers with facts in the knowledge base; the inference engine decides which question to ask next based on previous answers; it produces a diagnosis/list of possible diseases with probabilities; the explanation system shows the reasoning behind the conclusion; suggested treatment given.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any five valid points in a logical order.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how an expert system for diagnosing faults in mobile phones would be created.
parts.answer: Information is gathered from human experts (repair technicians) by interviews/questionnaires and from manuals/other sources; the knowledge base is created and populated with facts; a rules base of IF…THEN rules is created; the inference engine is designed/linked to the rules; the user interface is designed to ask questions and show results; an explanation system is included; the system is tested using faults with known solutions and results compared with the experts' diagnoses.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any five valid steps.

parts.label: b
parts.text: State two other applications of expert systems.
parts.answer: Any two: medical diagnosis; mineral/oil prospecting; car engine fault diagnosis; tax/financial advice; chess games; plant/animal identification; insurance or credit risk assessment.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give three advantages to customers of buying groceries through the internet.
parts.answer: Any three: no need to travel/saves fuel and time; can shop 24/7; goods are delivered to the home (useful for elderly/disabled people); easy to compare prices on different websites; can see a full range of products/reviews; fewer impulse purchases because a list is used.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one disadvantage to customers of internet shopping.
parts.answer: e.g. cannot see/feel goods before buying; risk of fraud/fake websites; delivery charges; delays in delivery; needs internet access and a bank card; returns can be difficult.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A supermarket in Islamabad uses an automatic stock control system linked to its checkouts. Describe how the stock level of an item is kept up to date and how new stock is ordered.
parts.answer: The bar code on the item is scanned at the checkout; the product code is used to search the stock database for the item's record; the price and description are sent back to the checkout; the stock level in the record is reduced by one (by the number sold); the new stock level is compared with the reorder level; if it is at or below the reorder level, an order is automatically sent to the supplier/flag set; the record is flagged as 'on order' so it is not reordered again; when new stock arrives, the stock level is increased.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any five valid points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The owner of a clothing shop in Hyderabad is closing her shop and selling only through her own online store. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages to the owner.
parts.answer: Advantages: no rent or shop running costs (electricity, staff); can sell to customers across the country/abroad 24/7; fewer staff needed; stock can be kept in a cheaper warehouse; customer data collected for targeted marketing; can update prices/offers instantly. Disadvantages: cost of building and maintaining a secure website; must pay for delivery/packaging and handle returns; loses passing customers who browse in person; customers cannot try clothes on so more returns; risk of hacking/fraud; staff may need retraining or lose jobs; strong competition from large online sellers. Conclusion.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A student reads a history textbook as an eBook on a tablet. Give two features of the eBook that are not available in the printed book.
parts.answer: Any two: words can be searched; text size can be changed; hyperlinks to other pages/websites/glossary; embedded video/audio/animations; built-in dictionary; bookmarks and notes that can be removed/edited easily; can be read aloud by text-to-speech; can be read in the dark (backlit).
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one disadvantage of the eBook compared with the printed book.
parts.answer: e.g. needs a charged device; screen can cause eye strain; device is expensive/can be stolen or damaged; may be harder to share or lend.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A publisher in Lahore is deciding whether to publish its monthly science magazine as an ePublication instead of on paper. Describe two advantages and two disadvantages to the publisher of the ePublication.
parts.answer: Advantages: no printing, paper or distribution costs; can reach readers worldwide instantly; can include video, animations and hyperlinks; can be updated/corrected after release; data on readers can be collected. Disadvantages: readers without devices or internet access are lost; easier to copy and share illegally; cost of developing for different devices/formats; some readers prefer paper so sales may fall; advertisers may pay less.
parts.working: 1 mark each for two advantages and two disadvantages (expanded).

parts.label: a
parts.text: A provincial health department wants to make people aware of a new polio vaccination drive. It is considering a website, printed posters and a social media campaign. Evaluate the use of these three methods for this purpose.
parts.answer: Website: can hold detailed information, maps of centres and video; can be updated; but people must know about it and have internet access. Posters: seen by everyone passing, including people without internet or phones; good in rural areas/clinics; but limited information, cannot be updated once printed, cost of printing and distribution, can be damaged. Social media: reaches many people quickly, especially young people; can be shared and targeted to areas; cheap; interactive (questions answered); but misinformation and negative comments can spread; does not reach people without smartphones; older people may not use it. Reasoned conclusion, e.g. a combination is best.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid evaluative point (benefit or drawback) about the methods, up to 5; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion. Max 4 if only one method discussed.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A customer inserts her bank card into an ATM and asks to withdraw Rs 10 000. Describe the processing that takes place after she has entered her PIN.
parts.answer: The PIN entered is compared with the PIN stored on the card chip/bank's records; if it is wrong the customer is asked to try again (card retained after three failed attempts); the bank's computer is contacted to check that the card is valid/not stolen; the account balance is checked to see that there are enough funds; the daily withdrawal limit is checked; if all checks are passed, the cash is dispensed and the account is debited by Rs 10 000; a receipt may be printed.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four processing steps. Do not credit descriptions of input or output devices.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Many shops in Pakistan now accept contactless card payments. Describe how a contactless payment is made.
parts.answer: The customer holds the card/phone close to the reader (within a few centimetres); data is transmitted wirelessly using RFID/NFC; payment is authorised (usually without a PIN for small amounts) and the amount is deducted from the account.
parts.working: 1 mark: card held near reader. 1 mark: RFID/NFC wireless transfer and payment authorised.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one advantage and one disadvantage to the customer of contactless payments.
parts.answer: Advantage: faster at the checkout; no need to enter a PIN; no need to carry cash. Disadvantage: a stolen card can be used for small payments without a PIN; easy to spend more than intended; risk of the card being read by a hidden reader (skimming).
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A bank is encouraging its customers to use internet banking instead of visiting branches. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages to customers of internet banking.
parts.answer: Advantages: can bank at any time from anywhere; no travel costs or queuing; easy to check balances and statements; transfers and bill payments made instantly; useful for disabled or elderly people who find travel difficult; alerts for transactions. Disadvantages: needs internet access and a device; risk of phishing/pharming/hacking and fraud; less personal service/cannot discuss problems face to face; easy to make a mistake with account numbers; some customers (elderly) lack skills/confidence; branch closures affect those who cannot use internet banking; social isolation. Conclusion.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point; 1 mark for reasoned conclusion. Answers must be about customers, not the bank.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the difference between optical mark recognition (OMR) and optical character recognition (OCR), giving a suitable use for each.
parts.answer: OMR detects marks (shaded boxes/lines) in set positions on a pre-printed form, e.g. multiple-choice exam answer sheets, lottery tickets, school registers. OCR reads printed or handwritten characters from a scanned image and converts them into text that can be edited/stored, e.g. reading passports at airports, digitising printed documents, number plate recognition.
parts.working: 1 mark: OMR description. 1 mark: OMR use. 1 mark: OCR description. 1 mark: OCR use.

parts.label: a
parts.text: A shopping mall car park in Karachi uses automatic number plate recognition (ANPR) to record when cars enter and leave. Describe how ANPR is used when a car arrives at the entrance barrier.
parts.answer: A sensor (e.g. pressure/infrared) detects the car arriving; a camera captures an image of the front of the car; software locates the number plate in the image (and adjusts brightness/contrast); OCR is used to identify the individual characters; the registration number is stored in a database with the date and time of entry; the barrier is raised (actuator) and an LED display may show a welcome message; when the car leaves, the plate is read again and the time difference used to calculate the charge.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any five valid steps in sequence.

parts.label: a
parts.text: City planners in Lahore use a computer model to test the effect of new traffic lights at a busy junction before installing them. Give three advantages of using a computer model.
parts.answer: Any three: cheaper than building/testing the real junction; safer — no risk of accidents to real drivers; many different 'what if' scenarios/timings can be tried quickly; time can be speeded up so years of traffic can be simulated quickly; no disruption to real traffic; easy to change the variables and compare results.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why the results of the model might not match what happens in reality.
parts.answer: The model is only as good as the data and rules used — real drivers' behaviour, accidents, weather or events may not be included/may be unpredictable.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: a
parts.text: The government uses a computer model to predict flooding along the River Indus during the monsoon. Describe how the model could be used to help plan for floods.
parts.answer: Data such as rainfall, river levels, ground height, dam releases and past floods are entered; 'what if' questions are asked, e.g. what if rainfall is 30% above average; the model predicts which areas will flood and when; planners can use the predictions to decide where to build embankments, when to warn and evacuate people and where to place relief supplies.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any three valid points.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the predictions of a flood model may be inaccurate.
parts.answer: Any two: the model is a simplification of reality; input data may be incomplete or inaccurate (e.g. faulty sensors, rainfall forecasts); unexpected events such as embankment failure may not be included; the rules/formulas may be based on past events that do not represent the future (e.g. climate change).
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe how a satellite navigation (satnav) system in a delivery van works out the van's position and guides the driver.
parts.answer: The satnav receives signals from (at least three/four) GPS satellites; each signal includes the time it was sent; the satnav calculates its distance from each satellite from the time taken for the signal to arrive; the position is found by comparing the distances (trilateration); the position is shown on a stored map; the computer calculates a route to the destination and gives spoken/visual directions.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four valid points.

parts.label: a
parts.text: State what is meant by a geographic information system (GIS).
parts.answer: A computer system that captures, stores, analyses and displays data linked to geographical locations (maps) in layers.
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give three uses of a GIS.
parts.answer: Any three: emergency services planning routes/locating incidents; planning new roads, schools or hospitals; mapping flood risk or disease outbreaks; environmental agencies monitoring forests/wildlife; utility companies mapping pipes and cables; police mapping crime hotspots; telecom companies planning mast locations.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Patients in an intensive care unit are monitored by computers with sensors. Name two sensors that could be used.
parts.answer: Any two: temperature sensor; pressure sensor (blood pressure); pulse/heart-rate sensor; oxygen (oximeter) sensor; respiration/breathing sensor.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two advantages of using computers rather than nurses to monitor these patients.
parts.answer: Any two: readings taken continuously, 24/7, without breaks; more accurate readings/no human error; alarms sound immediately if readings go outside safe limits; readings stored and displayed as graphs automatically; nurses are freed to carry out other tasks; several patients monitored at once.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe two ways in which 3D printers are used in medicine.
parts.answer: Any two: making prosthetic limbs (artificial hands/legs) designed to fit an individual; making implants such as bone/joint or dental implants; making models of a patient's organs so surgeons can plan operations; making personalised medical tools; tissue engineering/printing artificial tissue (research).
parts.working: 1 mark each for two described uses.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain two benefits to patients of prosthetic limbs made by 3D printing.
parts.answer: Any two: custom-made from scans to fit the individual exactly, so more comfortable; much cheaper than traditional prosthetics, so more affordable; quick to produce, so children can easily get replacements as they grow; can be made in local clinics/remote areas.
parts.working: 1 mark each for an explained benefit.

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: State three functions of an operating system.
parts.answer: Any three: manages memory; manages the processor/multitasking; manages input and output devices (peripherals) using drivers; manages files and folders (file management); provides a user interface; handles security/user accounts and passwords; handles interrupts and errors; loads/runs application software.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name the type of user interface described in each statement.
(i) The user types commands such as copy report.txt backup at a prompt.
(ii) The user clicks icons and chooses options from menus using a pointer.
(iii) The user says 'call home' to a phone, which carries out the action.
(iv) The user waves a hand in front of a smart TV's camera to change the channel.
parts.answer: (i) command line interface (CLI) (ii) graphical user interface (GUI) (iii) dialogue-based interface (iv) gesture-based interface
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe a command line interface.
parts.answer: The user types instructions/commands using a keyboard at a prompt; commands must be in an exact format/syntax and the computer responds with text output.
parts.working: 1 mark: typed commands. 1 mark: exact syntax/text-only display.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two advantages and two disadvantages of a command line interface compared with a graphical user interface.
parts.answer: Advantages: the user can access/configure everything directly, giving more control; uses less memory and processing power; commands can be combined/run as scripts to automate tasks; faster for expert users. Disadvantages: many commands must be learnt/remembered; commands must be typed exactly so errors are easy to make; difficult for beginners; no pictures/icons so less intuitive.
parts.working: 1 mark each for two advantages and two disadvantages.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A car has a dialogue-based interface for controlling the radio, phone and satnav. Describe how a dialogue-based interface works.
parts.answer: The user speaks commands into a microphone; voice recognition software compares the words with stored commands and carries out the action, often replying with speech.
parts.working: 1 mark: spoken commands via microphone. 1 mark: recognised/compared with stored commands and action carried out.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one advantage and one disadvantage of using this interface while driving.
parts.answer: Advantage: the driver keeps hands on the wheel and eyes on the road, so it is safer. Disadvantage: background noise or accents may not be recognised; limited set of commands; the driver may still be distracted.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare a dialogue-based interface with a gesture-based interface.
parts.answer: Similarities: both are natural/intuitive ways to give commands without a keyboard or mouse; both allow hands-free or touch-free control (e.g. of a smart TV or car system); both rely on software to recognise the input and compare it with stored commands; both can misinterpret input and have a limited set of commands that must be learnt. Differences: a dialogue-based interface uses spoken commands picked up by a microphone, whereas a gesture-based interface uses body/hand movements detected by a camera or motion sensors; a dialogue-based interface is affected by background noise and accents, whereas a gesture-based interface is affected by poor lighting or the user being out of the camera's view; a dialogue-based interface lets the user keep hands on another task (e.g. driving), whereas gestures need the hands/body to move; gestures can be used in noisy places or where speaking is unsuitable, whereas speech cannot.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid comparative point, up to 5; at least one similarity and one difference needed for full marks. Points must link the two interfaces, not be two separate lists.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe one advantage and one disadvantage of a gesture-based interface on a smart television.
parts.answer: Advantage: no remote control is needed so it cannot be lost; natural/intuitive movements so easy for young children; hygienic as nothing is touched. Disadvantage: unintended movements may be read as commands; the user must learn/remember the gestures; may not work well in poor light or if the user is out of the camera's view; can be tiring to use.
parts.working: 1 mark for each advantage/disadvantage, 1 mark each for its expansion (2 + 2).

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A technician manages 300 computers on a school network. She can use either a command line interface or a graphical user interface. Discuss which type of interface would be better for her work.
parts.answer: CLI: can write scripts to carry out the same task (e.g. installing updates, creating user accounts) on all 300 computers automatically; direct access to system settings; uses fewer resources so works on remote/low-powered machines; faster for an expert; but she must remember exact commands and a typing error could damage many machines. GUI: easier to learn and see the effects; fewer errors through choosing from menus; visual tools can show the network clearly; but repetitive tasks on 300 machines are slow, needs more memory, some settings may not be available. Conclusion: CLI is likely better for an experienced technician doing repetitive network tasks, perhaps with GUI tools for occasional jobs.
parts.working: Max 4 if only one interface discussed. 1 mark per expanded point applied to the scenario; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A graphical user interface is often called a WIMP interface. State what each letter of WIMP stands for.
parts.answer: Windows, Icons, Menus, Pointer (or pointing device)
parts.working: 2 marks all four; 1 mark for two or three.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one reason why a GUI is suitable for a young child using a computer for the first time.
parts.answer: The child does not need to learn/type commands — they can click/tap pictures (icons) that are easy to recognise.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Smartphones use a post-WIMP interface. Explain how the interface of a smartphone differs from the WIMP interface of a desktop computer.
parts.answer: A smartphone uses a touch screen, so fingers replace the mouse pointer; actions are made with gestures such as tap, swipe, pinch to zoom and rotate, which WIMP does not use; there are usually no overlapping windows — apps fill the whole screen; icons are larger so they can be pressed with a finger; menus are often hidden or replaced by on-screen buttons.
parts.working: 1 mark each for any four valid explained differences.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give two advantages of a desktop computer compared with a laptop for a family's home use.
parts.answer: Any two: usually cheaper for the same specification; easier to upgrade/repair parts; full-size keyboard and larger monitor are more comfortable; less likely to be stolen or dropped; better cooling so less overheating; often more powerful.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare a phablet with a smartphone.
parts.answer: Similarities: both can make calls and send messages; both have touch screens, internet access, cameras and run apps; both are portable and use mobile networks. Differences: a phablet has a larger screen than a smartphone (between a phone and a tablet); a phablet is easier for reading and watching video; a smartphone is smaller and lighter so fits in a pocket more easily; a phablet usually has a bigger battery but uses more power; a phablet is harder to use with one hand.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid comparative point up to 4; at least one similarity and one difference for full marks.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Census workers in rural Sindh use tablet computers to record household information. Give two advantages and two disadvantages of using tablets for this work.
parts.answer: Advantages: light and portable, easy to carry between houses; long battery life; touch screen with on-screen forms that can validate data; data can be sent to the central database immediately via mobile network; built-in camera/GPS records location. Disadvantages: touch screen typing slower than a keyboard; small screen; can be stolen or damaged; battery may run out with no charging point; poor mobile signal in remote areas prevents sending data.
parts.working: 1 mark each for two advantages and two disadvantages applied to the scenario.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A secondary school in Islamabad plans to replace the desktop computers in its computer room with laptops that students can also take to other classrooms. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of this plan.
parts.answer: Advantages: laptops can be used in any classroom, so ICT can be used in other subjects; take up less space; use less electricity; can work during power cuts using batteries; can connect wirelessly to the network; students can work in groups anywhere. Disadvantages: more expensive for the same performance; easier to steal or drop/damage; batteries wear out and need charging/charging trolleys; smaller screens and keyboards may cause poor posture; harder to upgrade/repair; Wi-fi may be slower than wired connections; can overheat. Conclusion.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Give three uses of a smartphone other than making phone calls.
parts.answer: Any three: sending text/instant messages; accessing the internet/browsing; sending emails; taking photos/videos; using satnav/maps; online banking/payments; social media; playing games/music; video calling; using apps such as a calculator or calendar.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A university student is deciding whether to buy a tablet or a laptop for writing assignments and attending online lectures. Compare a tablet with a laptop for this student.
parts.answer: Similarities: both portable with batteries; both can connect to Wi-fi to attend online lectures; both have screens, cameras and microphones for video calls. Differences: a laptop has a physical keyboard and touchpad so typing long assignments is quicker, whereas a tablet relies on an on-screen keyboard; a tablet is lighter and smaller so easier to carry; a laptop usually has more storage and processing power and runs full versions of software; a tablet usually has longer battery life; a laptop has more ports (USB) for connecting devices.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid comparative point up to 5; at least one similarity and one difference; points must relate the two devices.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe two features of a laptop computer that make it suitable for a salesperson who travels between cities.
parts.answer: Any two: lightweight and portable with a built-in keyboard, screen and touchpad (all in one unit); runs on a rechargeable battery so it can be used on trains/in hotels without mains power; built-in Wi-fi to connect to networks; built-in webcam for video conferencing.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two disadvantages of laptops for the salesperson.
parts.answer: Any two: easily stolen or lost when travelling; battery needs recharging/runs out; can be damaged if dropped; can overheat; small keyboard/screen can cause strain over long periods.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Name the type of computer described in each statement.
(i) A large, powerful computer with a separate monitor, keyboard and mouse that stays in one place.
(ii) A thin, portable device with only a touch screen, larger than a phone, usually without a physical keyboard.
(iii) A device that combines the features of a smartphone and a tablet, with a screen larger than a typical phone.
parts.answer: (i) desktop computer (ii) tablet (iii) phablet
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Name the type of internal memory that holds the operating system, programs and data currently in use.
parts.answer: RAM (random access memory)
parts.working: 1 mark.

parts.label: b
parts.text: A student's computer becomes slow when several programs are open at the same time. Explain why adding more RAM could make the computer run faster.
parts.answer: More programs and data can be held in RAM at the same time, so less data has to be moved between RAM and backing storage (e.g. the hard disk), which is much slower to access.
parts.working: 1 mark: more programs/data can be stored in RAM at once. 1 mark: less swapping to/from slower backing storage.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State the purpose of each internal component.
(i) Central processing unit (CPU)
(ii) Network interface card (NIC)
(iii) Graphics card
(iv) Motherboard
parts.answer: (i) processes instructions/carries out calculations and controls the computer. (ii) allows the computer to connect to a network. (iii) processes image data and sends the output to the monitor/screen. (iv) the main circuit board that connects all components together and allows them to communicate.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare RAM and ROM.
parts.answer: Similarities: both are internal memory/directly accessed by the CPU; both are solid-state chips on the motherboard; both store data/instructions. Differences: RAM is volatile while ROM is non-volatile; RAM is read/write while ROM is read-only; RAM holds the OS, programs and data currently in use while ROM holds the boot program/BIOS; RAM is usually much larger in capacity.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid comparative point; at least one similarity and one difference for full marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why the instructions used to start up a computer are stored in ROM rather than RAM.
parts.answer: ROM is non-volatile so the instructions are still there when the computer is switched on (RAM is empty at start-up); ROM is read-only so the instructions cannot be accidentally erased or changed.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A washing machine contains a microprocessor and a small amount of ROM. Explain why the washing programmes (cycles) are stored in ROM.
parts.answer: The programmes must not be lost when the machine is switched off, so non-volatile ROM is needed; the user should not be able to change/erase them accidentally, so read-only memory is suitable.
parts.working: 1 mark: non-volatile. 1 mark: cannot be altered.

parts.label: b
parts.text: The washing machine also has some RAM. Suggest what might be stored in the RAM.
parts.answer: e.g. the current settings chosen by the user (temperature, spin speed, delay time); the current stage of the cycle/time remaining; sensor readings such as water level or temperature.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A journalist is typing a news report in a word processor when there is a power cut. She had last saved the report 20 minutes earlier. Explain what happens to her work and why.
parts.answer: While she types, the word processor and the open document are held in RAM; RAM is volatile, so its contents are lost when the power is cut; the work typed in the last 20 minutes is lost and only the version saved to backing storage (which is non-volatile) remains.
parts.working: 1 mark: document being edited is in RAM. 1 mark: RAM is volatile/contents lost. 1 mark: only saved copy on backing storage kept/last 20 minutes lost.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one way she could reduce the amount of work lost in future.
parts.answer: e.g. save more often / turn on the autosave (autorecover) option; use an uninterruptible power supply (UPS); use cloud software that saves continuously; use a laptop with a charged battery.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Describe the difference between virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR).
parts.answer: VR creates a completely computer-generated 3D environment that replaces the real world, usually seen through a headset. AR overlays computer-generated images/information onto the user's view of the real world, e.g. through a phone camera or glasses.
parts.working: 1 mark: VR = fully artificial environment replacing reality. 1 mark: AR = digital content added to the real world.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one example of a use of AR.
parts.answer: e.g. seeing how furniture would look in a room through a phone app; games such as catching virtual creatures in real places; showing directions on a car windscreen (head-up display); showing labels on museum exhibits; virtual try-on of glasses/clothes.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: An airline trains its pilots using virtual reality. Give three advantages of using VR for this training.
parts.answer: Any three: dangerous situations (engine failure, bad weather) can be practised safely; no risk to aircraft or passengers; cheaper than using real aircraft/no fuel used; scenarios can be repeated as many times as needed; the trainee's performance can be recorded and reviewed; training can take place at any time regardless of weather.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give one disadvantage of VR training.
parts.answer: e.g. headsets can cause motion sickness/headaches/eye strain; equipment is expensive; it may not feel exactly like the real situation.
parts.working: 1 mark.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) is used in many everyday applications. Describe two examples of AI being used in everyday life.
parts.answer: Any two, described: chatbots on websites answer customers' questions by understanding their messages; voice assistants recognise speech and answer questions/carry out commands; streaming and shopping websites recommend films or products based on what the user has watched/bought before; self-driving or driver-assist cars use sensors and AI to recognise road signs, lanes and obstacles; email spam filters learn to recognise spam; facial recognition to unlock phones.
parts.working: For each example: 1 mark for naming a valid use, 1 mark for describing how AI is involved.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: A furniture shop in Karachi is planning an augmented reality app that lets customers see how its sofas and tables would look in their own homes. Discuss the benefits and drawbacks of this app for the shop.
parts.answer: Benefits: customers can see the size, colour and fit of furniture in their own room before buying, so fewer returns; more confidence leads to more online sales; customers who cannot visit the shop can still choose; modern image attracts younger customers; fewer display models needed in the showroom. Drawbacks: expensive to develop and maintain the app and 3D models of every product; customers need a suitable smartphone; the app may show sizes or colours inaccurately, causing complaints; customers cannot feel the comfort or material; the app must be updated when stock changes. Conclusion.
parts.working: Max 4 for one side only. 1 mark per expanded point applied to the shop; 1 mark for a reasoned conclusion.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Explain the difference between hardware and software.
parts.answer: Hardware is the physical parts of a computer system that can be touched, e.g. keyboard, processor. Software is the programs/instructions that tell the computer what to do, e.g. an operating system, a word processor.
parts.working: 1 mark: hardware = physical components. 1 mark: software = programs/instructions.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Classify each of these as internal hardware or external hardware: motherboard, printer, RAM, monitor.
parts.answer: Internal: motherboard, RAM. External: printer, monitor.
parts.working: 2 marks all four; 1 mark for two or three.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text:
State whether each item is system software or application software:
(i) spreadsheet
(ii) compiler
(iii) photo editing software
(iv) device driver
(v) operating system
(vi) video editing software
parts.answer: System: compiler, device driver, operating system. Application: spreadsheet, photo editing software, video editing software.
parts.working: 3 marks all six correct; 2 marks four or five; 1 mark two or three.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text:
Describe the purpose of each type of system software.
(i) Device driver
(ii) Compiler
(iii) Utility software
parts.answer: (i) allows the operating system to communicate with/control a hardware device such as a printer. (ii) translates a whole program written in a high-level language into machine code so it can be run. (iii) carries out specific tasks to maintain/look after the computer, e.g. anti-virus, backup, defragmentation, compression.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Give two examples of utility software.
parts.answer: Any two: anti-virus; anti-spyware; backup; disk defragmenter; file compression; disk formatter; file management/security (encryption) software.
parts.working: 1 mark each.

author: HomiLabs

topic: Types and components of computer systems

parts.label: a
parts.text: Compare system software with application software.
parts.answer: Similarities: both are programs/instructions stored on the computer; both are needed for the user to do useful work. Differences: system software controls and manages the computer hardware and provides a platform for other software, whereas application software lets the user carry out specific tasks (e.g. writing letters); application software cannot run without system software (an operating system) but system software can run without applications; system software usually runs in the background, whereas the user interacts directly with application software; examples: operating system/compiler vs word processor/spreadsheet.
parts.working: 1 mark per valid comparative point; at least one similarity and one difference for full marks.

parts.label: b
parts.text: Explain why a new computer needs an operating system before the user can run a word processor.
parts.answer: The word processor relies on the operating system to manage memory, the processor, files and devices (e.g. keyboard, printer) and to provide the user interface; without the operating system the word processor cannot load or communicate with the hardware.
parts.working: 1 mark: OS manages hardware/resources for the application. 1 mark: application cannot be loaded/run or use devices without it.

author: HomiLabs
